question: Is Ghostty's VT core (libghostty-vt, via @coder/libghostty-vt-node) better than the xterm.js the pinned base ships, for the headless terminal state Caret would keep on the host/mobile path - and is adopting it safe?
answer: yes on the path it would be used: 25.7x throughput at realistic (8 KiB) chunk sizes, 4.5x less memory per live terminal, and a structured snapshot API xterm lacks; behaviourally identical on all 12 corpus cases. Safe to try: MIT, prebuilt for darwin-arm64, no install-time toolchain.

engines.candidate: @coder/libghostty-vt-node 0.1.0-beta.0, native info {napiVersion: 10, ghosttyVersion: '0.1.0-dev', platform: darwin, arch: arm64}

method.runtime: Node 24.18.0 (the runtime the Caret host bundles)
method.where: scratch directory outside the repository; only the corpus and its runner landed in the tree
method.payload: coloured log lines, CR progress redraws, cursor-addressed alternate-screen writes, CSI ?2026 frames, OSC 0 title, OSC 8 hyperlink, Thai lines with combining marks

feed_1_3MB_chunks.note: xterm faster when writes are huge

feed_8KiB_chunks.note: the shape a PTY reader actually delivers

conformance.corpus: 12 cases in apps/macos/src/terminal-conformance.ts (OSC 633/133, OSC 8, CSI ?2026, Thai combining, CJK width, box drawing, DECSC/DECRC, scroll region + RI, erase+CR, alt-screen round trip, ZWJ emoji recorded only)
conformance.note: the first runs failed 3 cases against my own expectations, not the engines: a bare LF keeps the column, an on-screen line is not an empty screen, and a reverse index keeps the moved line's column

landed: scripts/lib/terminal-engines.ts - xterm adapter (shipped engine) + optional Ghostty adapter (dynamic import)
scripts/terminal-conformance.ts and `bun run check:terminal` - the report
apps/macos/test/terminal-conformance.test.ts - the gate: required cases must hold on the shipped engine; also the acceptance test for any future swap
root devDependency @xterm/headless@6.1.0-beta.302 (same line as the desktop pin)
caveats: @coder/libghostty-vt-node is 0.1.0-beta.0 and upstream libghostty-vt has no tagged version and an unstable C API: pin the commit and treat updates as deliberate work
no Windows prebuild, and building from source needs Zig - fine for the macOS target, a gate before Windows
the visible terminal is untouched: the workbench still renders xterm.js, and Cursor does too, so replacing the renderer remains a section 5 deviation decision
single-run measurements on one machine: order-of-magnitude, not competitive benchmarking
